in all three cases. This proves command wiring/refusal, not a real consumer migration.

Adoption test binaries cross-compiled for linux/amd64 and windows/amd64 with
`CGO_ENABLED=0`. An initial Linux attempt inherited native macOS C tooling and failed;
the explicit pure-Go configuration removes that toolchain mismatch. Neither binary
was run on its target; no Linux/Windows behavior or G6 desktop support is certified.

## Source review beyond the inspector

Both apps use app-owned tokens/generated CSS and import shared Go/script behavior;
neither currently has a portable kit.lock. CA's compiled tw.css exists but is ignored;
GGB tracks its compiled CSS. A future selection must name actual required build outputs
without claiming they are all tracked, generated by kit defaults or portable-vendor files.

CA's CLAUDE.md has app-kit guidance, while its AGENTS.md does not. GGB's two files
currently carry Fathom guidance, not the app-kit router. Text identity alone would
therefore miss the shared omission; the selected routing check requires the canonical
app-kit block in both files, not merely equal file hashes.

## Working-tree shell refresh — same day

A later read-only source review found both apps already call `dashboard.RenderShell`,
`RenderNav` and `MatchPath`, plus `appearance.BootstrapScript` and `RenderControl`.
Their `internal/web/render.go` and browser/style files have existing modifications;
both `internal/web/render_test.go` files are untracked. These are working-tree
integrations, not released versions or changes authored by this refresh.

Source identities at review (HEAD alone does not identify the dirty files):

| Identity | Car Assistant | Growing Gardens BI |
|---|---|---|
| HEAD | `1f22fe59d795ea7b9f50856aaa4f4b99252f625c` | `7503dd1c270bf6ceb72d42c742f507b9513db0dc` |
| render.go SHA-256 | `679eb1574d1d803fad6a9f843e29aa0c8411f5938a792f9d37517fdd86b5b3c0` | `442a30ad45f6efbdd4f63959bec77cb0c3457a0c8832f372c3a67434fa8506c5` |
| render_test.go SHA-256 | `9908a7e9263a3cd965bec39286b6ea645189b332ce09db520200b9c082cb8dff` | `39d684e376b8b6d40d7870390b97aebd6f58841096d5c1114c5132d49fa5cc36` |

The shared `appkit/ui/dashboard/shell.go` renders a native mobile Menu disclosure
containing the same navigation as the desktop sidebar. CA retains app-owned bottom
quick links. A truncated index snippet omitted the disclosure; reading the full
renderer corrected the initial inference that mobile destinations were absent.
Discoverability, narrow-header overflow and keyboard behavior need browser observation;
there is no current evidence justifying another navigation rewrite.

CA's shopping profiles/chat and GGB's financial settings/Ask drawer remain app-owned.
GGB campaign routes use the inspected app-wide authentication boundary; this review
did not establish a separate campaign permission check. Navigation is not authorization.
App branding, destinations and appearance-control wrappers are composition seams,
not evidence of duplicated preference-state machinery.

In each app, this bounded synthetic suite passed without launching the application:

```sh
go test ./internal/web -run '^(TestNavigation|TestPageShell|TestAppearance)' -count=1
```

Each suite selected five tests: route matching, identity/grouping, skip links,
appearance runtime selection and redraw/CSS contracts. CA passed in 0.309s; GGB in
0.706s. Neither run establishes browser interaction, live authentication or delivery.
No consumer source, live data or deployment was changed. The previously approved
GGB finance/export repair was preserved.

Both apps still lack `appkit.adoption.json`, `docs/app-kit.md` and an intent router.
Their existing instructions—not invented kit policy—remain the consumer context.
The zero-version/local replacement and paired agent-guidance gaps above remain.

## Current disposition: owner-deferred

The owner has put both apps' adoption on hold as low priority under
[ADR-0032](../adr/0032-defer-car-assistant-and-growing-gardens-adoption.md).
Do not write consumer contracts/selections/routers, change their shells, set up hosts,
or repeat approval prompts for this work. Do not select other apps automatically.
The observations and approved GGB finance/export repair above remain historical evidence;
neither the deferral nor existing integrations complete G2/G3/G4 or certify delivery.

Resume only when the owner explicitly names the current app/task. Refresh its own
context, dirty files and authority before a reviewed contract/selection/router change.
Static checking, fresh Claude/Codex sessions, clean sibling-free builds and browser/task
proof remain separate requirements, as does reviewed second-consumer propagation.
Do not invent kit.lock provenance, an account backend or an immutable delivery revision.
